title: contingent-rollout-slate-and-metric-experiment-notes
content:
Purpose
This working doc captures a pragmatic rollout slate for incremental launches where we intentionally gate traffic, run metric experiments, and maintain fast rollback paths. Designed for product-ops + eng oncall + release leads.

Audience
- Product Ops (primary)
- Release Engineering
- Platform & SRE
- Solutions Eng for customer handoffs

Summary of approach (TL;DR)
1) Define a small set of primary KPIs and a compact experiment plan for each cohort.
2) Stage traffic by feature-flag cohorts with explicit SLO ramps and rollback thresholds.
3) Run a 72-hour burn window per cohort with predefined health probes, then promote or revert.
4) Keep runbook lightweight: 6 checks pre-traffic, 5 live probes, 3 post-promotion validations.

Primary KPIs (compact)
- Latency p50/p95 (ms) — route and model-level
- Error rate (%) — per-route and library (e.g., decoding, streaming timeouts)
- Cost per 1k tokens (USD) — expected vs actual
- Quality regression signal — automatic eval pass rate on canary prompt set
- User-facing degradation (support tickets / 1k requests)

Experiment buckets & definitions
- Bucket A (internal beta): 0.1% traffic, control model v1, monitor all metrics closely
- Bucket B (partner beta): 1% traffic, model v2-quantized, enable caching layer, compare quality and cost
- Bucket C (gradual public): 10% -> 25% -> 50% ramp over 7 days if signals green

72-hour burn window checks (live probes)
- Health probe: 1 synthetic request per min to each region (success >= 99% over 3h)
- Latency drift: p95 not exceeding baseline by >25% over hourly windows
- Error spike: sustained error rate >0.5% for 15m triggers alert
- Quality sentinel: automatic eval set drop >2% pass rate triggers manual review
- Cost anomaly: spend per minute > x1.6 baseline triggers investigation

Pre-launch checklist (Quick run)
- [ ] Feature-flag gate created with clear names and rollout IDs
- [ ] Canary prompt set loaded into Optimize and referenced in linked_artifacts
- [ ] Monitoring dashboards created: latency, errors, quality, cost per-token
- [ ] Incident channels and oncall roster confirmed for 72-hour window
- [ ] Rollback playbook published and linked in the feature flag description
- [ ] Customer comms template prepared (for partner betas)

Go / No-go decision heuristics (during burn window)
Green if: all primary KPIs within thresholds for 24h and no single severity-1 incident
Yellow if: one KPI outside threshold but improving trend and mitigations available -> extend observation and possibly reduce traffic
Red if: error rate or latency breach sustained for 15m OR quality regression >2% absolute -> immediate rollback to previous model variant

Escalation & contacts
- Launch lead: Avery Chen (owner) — pager: PG-101 
- SRE escalation: Diego Morales — slack: @diegom 
- Product escalation: Maya Thompson — slack: @maya 
- Exec notify list (email) maintained in linked_artifacts

Metric experiment templates (instructions)
- For each KPI define: hypothesis, metric, statistical test, minimum sample size, burn window, success threshold.
Example: hypothesis — quantized model lowers cost by >=20% with <1% quality loss.
Metric — cost per 1k tokens; Quality — eval pass rate difference.
Test — two-sample proportion test on pass rates; Minimum requests: 10k for partner bucket.

Operations knobs (quick reference)
- Throttle: reduce cohort traffic by 10x via flag if p95 > threshold
- Freeze rollout: stop traffic adds but keep existing traffic steady for triage
- Rollback: toggle flag to previous variant and run 30m health hold before promotion retries

Observability items to create before traffic
- Per-model latency p50/p95 heatmap by region
- Token-level cost breakdown (tokenization, decoding, network egress)
- Canary prompt set quality dashboard with per-prompt diffs and highlight of hallucinations
- Alerting rules: composite alerts that require two signals (latency + errors) to reduce noise

Short-term followups (TODOs)
- [ ] Add A/B assignment metadata to telemetry (owner: Ravi Patel)
- [ ] Bake in automatic rollback rule for partner betas (owner: Avery)
- [ ] Run a tabletop for the rollback sequence with SRE (owner: Diego)
- [ ] Add churn metric for token cache hit rate to Optimize suggestions (owner: Maya)

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep checklist minimal — teams skip long docs. Prefer checkboxes in the console route config.
- For highly regulated customers run a parallel private rollout plan in Private env with explicit audit logs.
- Consider a quick toggle to disable caching if quality regressions correlate with cache hits.

Appendix: quick sample burn-window timeline (hourly slices)
- Hour 0: enable bucket at target traffic; sanity health probes + notify oncall
- Hour 1-3: monitor hourly windows; run initial quality eval at 3h mark
- Hour 6: interim review; if green, continue, else throttle or rollback
- Hour 24: 1-day decision checkpoint
- Hour 48-72: extended observations and final promotion if green

References and links (see linked_artifacts for primary anchors)
- Confluence playbook (linked)
- Jira: PROJ-3421, PROJ-3470 (feature flags + canary prompts)
- GitHub toggle repo and PRs
- Slack thread: #prod-launch-ops

End notes
This doc is a working slate — copy into the release checklist template before each launch and adapt cohort sizes to the traffic profile. Leave inline notes if you deviate from the plan so we can iterate the playbook.
